description: The bar chart, titled "Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models," illustrates the performance of four different models—mBERT-targ, XLM-targ, mBERT-permute, and XLM-permute—across eight language families: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis represents the "effect" score, ranging from 0 to 40, with error bars indicating variability. The horizontal axis lists the language families, with the IE-other category having a grey bar, likely indicating a different data type or baseline. For each language family, four bars are displayed, each corresponding to one of the models as defined in the legend. The mBERT-targ model (light blue) generally shows the highest effect scores, particularly in the IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, and Uralic groups, where its scores exceed 20. The XLM-targ model (dark blue) consistently performs second, with scores often between 10 and 25. The mBERT-permute (light green) and XLM-permute (dark green) models show the lowest performance, with effect scores mostly below 10. The chart shows that the mBERT-targ model consistently outperforms the other three models across all language families, while the XLM-targ model is the second best. The mBERT-permute and XLM-permute models show the lowest effect scores, with the XLM-permute model generally performing slightly worse than the mBERT-permute model.
